Protein
The need for protein decreases from approximately 1.1 g/kg in 
early childhood to 0.95 g/kg in late childhood (Table 17-1). Pro-
tein intake can range from 5% to 30% of total energy, depending 
on age. Protein deficiency is uncommon in American children, 
partly because of the cultural emphasis on high-protein foods. 
National surveys show that less than 3% of children fail to meet 
the recommended dietary allowance. Children who are most at 
risk for inadequate protein intake are those on strict vegan diets,
